brief.subject: Diesel jumps 9.7 cents to $6.276 as fuel tops trucking worries
brief.headline: Diesel climbs 9.7 cents to $6.276; fuel tops ATRI's list of trucking concerns
brief.dek: Diesel rebounds after a four-week slide, safety blitzes write hundreds of violations, and a $47M verdict lands in New Mexico.
brief.lede: The national diesel average rose 9.7 cents to $6.276 per gallon, snapping a stretch that still leaves prices down 25.3 cents over four weeks.

sections.heading: Diesel bounces back up
bullets: $6.276 per gallon is the new U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-10-19.
Up 9.7 cents (1.6%) from last week, so check fuel surcharges on loads booked at older rates.
Still down 25.3 cents over four weeks, but the reversal is a reminder to budget for swings.

sections.heading: Fuel is trucking's top worry
bullets: Fuel prices ranked No. 1 in ATRI's annual top-issues survey after missing the top 10 the prior two years.
Drivers ranked fuel first and carriers ranked it second, showing cost pressure is felt across the industry.

sections.heading: Enforcement and fraud crackdowns
bullets: Hundreds of violations and out-of-service orders came from recent CDL blitzes from California to North Dakota.
A Massachusetts man faces up to 15 years over a $3,000 Bluetooth CDL exam cheating scheme.
$30.4M in suspected meth was found in a commercial salt load at Laredo, keeping border inspections tight.

sections.heading: Nuclear verdict in New Mexico
bullets: $47 million was awarded by a jury to a pickup driver and his mother after a 2022 tanker crash near Carlsbad.
Verdicts this size keep pressure on insurance premiums for small fleets.

sections.heading: Labor policy and equipment shifts
bullets: The 2026 elections will reshape trucking labor policy regardless of which party wins, experts told an ATA committee.
Independent contractor rules may no longer split neatly along party lines, a key issue for leased owner-operators.
Daimler is building autonomy hardware into Freightliner trucks at the factory while leaving the software choice open.
